assertions.name: g_A_vs_PDG_2024
assertions.source: PDG 2024 (compared to derived value from H_3(q) conjugation)

description: Computation of g_A from the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_3(q). The Borromean braid β = σ₁σ₂⁻¹σ₁σ₂⁻¹ is conjugated with the single-strand conversion operator σ₁ to model the d→u weak vertex on the Borromean nucleon. KNOWN STRUCTURAL GAP: any conjugation β·σ·β⁻¹ has the same trace as σ by trace-cyclicity, so the suppression factor is forced to be 1.0 and the script can only output the naive g_A = 5/3 ≈ 1.667 (+30.6% vs PDG 1.2754). The right operator requires the full colored Markov trace with Wedderburn-block weights; see audit doc GT-MATRIX gap and y-lambda-jones-markov-witness.json for the canonical recipe.

data.interpretation: The Borromean braid β = σ₁σ₂⁻¹σ₁σ₂⁻¹ in H_3(q) conjugates the conversion operator σ₁. The suppression factor is the ratio of the standard-rep trace (with Borromean) to the standard-rep trace (without). By trace-cyclicity tr(βσβ⁻¹) = tr(σ), so this ratio is forced to 1.0; g_A reduces to the naive 5/3. Closure of the +30.6% gap requires the colored Markov trace, not a conjugation.

caveats: The Borromean correction operator β·σ₁·β⁻¹ is a CONJUGATION; by trace-cyclicity its trace equals tr(σ₁), so the 'suppression factor' is forced to be exactly 1.0 in any matrix representation. The +30.6% gap vs PDG is therefore structural, not numerical.
The exact Borromean braid word for the nucleon is model-dependent. Multiple candidate braids are evaluated above (data.braid_candidates).
The spin-isospin Clebsch-Gordan factor is taken from the naive quark model (5/3 = 4/3 + 1/3).
A full computation requires the colored Markov trace with Wedderburn-block weights, not just the standard representation. See audit doc 2026-05-04-deep-mass-beta-binding-audit.md GT-MATRIX.
